plan: To maximize profit, bid slightly above the midpoint of the value range. My value is $13, so a reasonable bid is around $11. This balances the risk of overpaying with the chance of winning. Since the values are random each round, other bidders may have lower values and bid less. By bidding $11, I aim to win while ensuring a profit margin if the second-highest bid is lower.

As my value for the prize is $9, I aim to maximize profit by ensuring I win if the price is below $9. To do this, I should bid slightly over $9 to account for competition, such as $9.1. This ensures I remain in the auction until the price reaches my value. If competitors bid below $9.1, I win and gain profit. If they bid higher, I exit without loss. This strategy balances winning potential with profit maximization.

Given my private value of $8, I aim to maximize profit by setting a bid slightly below my value, say $7.5, to leave a margin for profit. This bid allows me to potentially win if others undervalue or bid conservatively. I avoid bidding too high to ensure I maintain a positive profit margin if I win. As this is the only round, I rely on this strategy without historical data.
